::: {#brief .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-sb-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The brief</p>
<dl class="lx-sb-facts">
<div><dt>The nation</dt><dd>Prairieland (fictional): <b>20 million</b> people in <b>five regions</b> joined by seven links; oil imported through one strait; all its coal mined in Ridge County.</dd></div>
<div><dt>You decide</dt><dd>How fast buildings, transport and industry switch to electricity; a <span class="lx-term" data-term="carbon-budget">cumulative carbon budget</span>; an import cap; what the model may build or retire; a shock; the costs, within fixed ranges.</dd></div>
<div><dt>The engine works out</dt><dd>One <span class="lx-term" data-term="linear-program">linear program (LP)</span> picks what to build, run and retire in each region for 2030, 2035, 2040, 2045 and 2050 at the least <span class="lx-term" data-term="present-value">present value</span> of cost, on twelve <span class="lx-term" data-term="time-slice">time slices</span> of 2025's weather.</dd></div>
<div><dt>It leaves out</dt><dd>Power-flow physics, outages, end-use equipment costs, fuels other than electricity for the oil that remains, and who decides: a teaching model, not a forecast.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Units</dt><dd>Power in MW and GW; energy in TWh and PJ (1 TWh = 3.6 PJ); CO₂ in Mt, million tonnes. Fuel prices per GJ on <span class="lx-term" data-term="net-calorific-value">net calorific values</span>.</dd></div>
<div><dt>Short forms</dt><dd>O&amp;M: operation and maintenance. <span class="lx-term" data-term="lng">LNG</span>: liquefied natural gas, imported by ship. t per TJ: tonnes of CO₂ per terajoule of fuel.</dd></div>
</dl>
<p class="lx-hint">Open-ended: start from a preset, change one thing at a time, and copy the plan link to keep a plan. Prairieland is fictional; its numbers are illustrative.</p>
</div>
```
:::

```{=html}
</ul></div>
```

## How the engine works, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="sb4-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Decisions</dt><dd>What to build in each region and model year, what to retire early, which links to widen, how to run every slice, and which fuels to buy.</dd>
<dt>Goal</dt><dd>The least present value of cost 2026–2050, with each plant paying only for the years it runs up to 2050 (its residual value is not charged).</dd>
<dt>Rules</dt><dd>Each region-slice balances; plants within their limits; links within theirs; CO₂ summed over the years within the budget; imports within the cap; the stress hours met.</dd>
<dt>It holds when</dt><dd>Twelve slices of 2025's weather stand for every year; costs stay the same whatever is built; electrification follows the plan.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The linear program behind the bench</summary>

```

- **The model, written down:** [M13](m13-national-pathway.html): vintages, residual value, the budget, the import cap, foresight and the full-year check.
- **The same LP in Python:** M13's notebook, with SciPy and HiGHS.
- **A pathway defended:** the capstone [C4](c4-prairieland-2050.html), on this engine.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>When two answers cost the same: the tie rule and penalties</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<p>Small stated costs, left out of every reported number, pick one plan when several cost the same:</p>
<ul class="sb4-rules">
<li>$0.05 per MWh carried on any link, so power does not wander between regions;</li>
<li>$0.50 per MWh out of a battery, so it does not cycle for nothing;</li>
<li>$0.01 per GJ more for imported crude than domestic crude, so domestic crude is used first.</li>
</ul>
<p>Penalties keep every run solvable and are never part of a reported cost:</p>
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts sb4-pen"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Rule broken</th><th scope="col">Unit</th><th scope="col">Penalty</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Electricity not served</td><td>MWh</td><td class="n">$10,000</td></tr>
<tr><td>Short at a stress hour</td><td>MW for a year</td><td class="n">$750,000</td></tr>
<tr><td>CO₂ over the budget</td><td>tonne</td><td class="n">$1,000</td></tr>
<tr><td>Imports over the cap</td><td>GJ</td><td class="n">$100</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p>The budget and the cap are limits, not prices. A run that misses either is solved twice more: first for the least overshoot, serving no less demand; then for the least cost at that overshoot.</p>
<p>So "out of reach" means no plan within your levers meets the limit; the run shown is the closest.</p>
<p>A check on the default plan: plans within $1,000 of its best cost build the same national wind, solar, gas and firm capacity in 2030, 2040 and 2050, within 10 MW (the engine's test). That covers those totals only, not regions or links.</p>
<p>The tie rule picks one answer; it does not make it the only one. Within a millionth of the cost, 2046–2050's new solar can move by a gigawatt or more (<a href="m13-national-pathway.html">M13</a>, step 11).</p>
```

```{=html}
<li>Cole, W., Ramasamy, V. and Turan, M. (2025). <a href="https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy25osti/93281.pdf">Cost Projections for Utility-Scale Battery Storage: 2025 Update</a> (PDF). NREL/TP-6A40-93281. Only its 2024 cost, in 2025 dollars, as the low end of the battery range.</li>
<li>Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (2006). <a href="https://www.ipcc.ch/report/2006-ipcc-guidelines-for-national-greenhouse-gas-inventories/">2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Volume 2: Energy</a>, chapters 1 and 2.</li>
<li>U.S. Energy Information Administration. <a href="https://www.eia.gov/electricity/gridmonitor/">Hourly Electric Grid Monitor (Form EIA-930)</a>, Southwest Power Pool, 2025 and 2024 (accessed 2 and 3 Nov 2026).</li>
<li>International Energy Agency. <a href="https://www.iea.org/statistics-questionnaires-faq">Statistics questionnaires FAQ</a>: the physical energy content method (read 7 Nov 2026).</li>
<li>DeCarolis, J., et al. (2017). <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2017.03.001">Formalizing best practice for energy system optimization modelling</a>. Applied Energy, 194, 184–198.</li>
<li>Huangfu, Q., and Hall, J. A. J. (2018). <a href="https://doi.org/10.1007/s12532-017-0130-5">Parallelizing the dual revised simplex method</a>. Mathematical Programming Computation, 10, 119–142 (the HiGHS solver).</li>
</ul>
</div>
```
